title: The house filled with the odor (John 12:1–8)
hook: Mary of Bethany anoints his feet with costly nard

segments.voice: Yesterday, anastasis, and Martha meeting Jesus on the road. Your line was love with nowhere to go.

A scent doesn't stay politely in one corner. It fills a room, gets into curtains, follows people home on their clothes. Long after the guests have gone, a house can still smell of the dinner. Six days before the Passover, Jesus is back in Bethany at a dinner, and Lazarus, the man who was dead, is sitting at the table. Then his sister Mary opens a jar, and nobody in the house can miss what happens next.
screen: `A SCENT WON'T STAY PUT.` → `SIX DAYS BEFORE THE PASCH.` → `DINNER IN BETHANY.`

segments.voice: Martha is serving; Lazarus is at the table. And Mary takes a pound of ointment, spikenard, of great price, John says. She pours it on Jesus's feet and wipes them with her hair. Then John adds one sentence that's pure memory, as if he can still smell it. The Douay-Rheims says: "and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment." Odour is the British spelling of odor, and here it just means fragrance. Judas objects: why wasn't this sold for three hundred pence and given to the poor? A penny there is a denarius, roughly a day's pay for a laborer, so this jar is worth three hundred days of a laborer's pay, poured out in a minute. John says plainly that Judas didn't care about the poor; he kept the purse and helped himself. Jesus defends her: let her alone, she has kept it for the day of my burial. Then: "For the poor you have always with you; but me you have not always." People sometimes hear that as a shrug about poverty. Readers who know Deuteronomy hear an echo instead: the poor will not be wanting in the land, it says, and so open your hand to them. Read that way, Jesus is saying, this moment won't come again. Mary seems to understand what the others don't: he is about to die. So she does something extravagant, physical and unforgettable.
screen: `MARTHA SERVES, LAZARUS EATS.` · `A POUND OF NARD, POURED.` · `THREE HUNDRED PENCE, AND JUDAS.` · `KEPT FOR MY BURIAL.` · then, large: `THE HOUSE FILLED WITH THE ODOR.`

segments.voice: Breathe slowly through your nose a few times and notice what you can smell right now, even faintly. Then think of one person and one generous thing they would notice, flowers on a table, bread warming, a candle lit, a handwritten note, and let it become concrete in your mind. If you pray, offer it the way Mary offered the jar; if not, just hold the person in mind.
Nard. The costly perfume Mary of Bethany poured on Jesus's feet, filling the whole house with its fragrance. Today's word.
Your line: the whole house knew. A gift poured out doesn't stay in its corner. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: The Church reads the anointing at Bethany at Mass on the Monday of Holy Week.

chat.says: Jesus said "the poor you have always with you." Does that mean he didn't care about them?
options: Readers hear Deuteronomy's open your hand; he meant this moment before his death won't come again.
He meant giving to the poor was pointless, since poverty would never end anyway.
He agreed with Judas that the perfume should have been sold for the poor.
chat.meaning: Jesus defends Mary: she kept it for my burial. Read with Deuteronomy, the line says this moment won't come again, not that the poor don't matter.

spikenard.meaning: a costly perfumed ointment, also called nard

Bethany.meaning: the village of Martha, Mary and Lazarus

denarius.meaning: a coin, roughly a day's pay for a laborer

Deuteronomy.meaning: a book of the Law: open your hand to the poor

sources.quoted: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment.

notes: Spikenard from Nardostachys jatamansi, native to the Himalayas. Confirm.
Three hundred pence as close to a year's wages (denarius as a day's pay, Matthew 20:2). Confirm framing.
John 12:1–11 as the Gospel of Monday of Holy Week. Confirm.
Western tradition at times identified Mary of Bethany with Mary Magdalene; deliberately not raised here. Keeper may wish to add a note.
